title: NVIDIA Maxwell (Tesla M10, M40) on an ARM host
examples: Tesla M10 on an RK3588 board

inference.summary: llama.cpp with CUDA 12.9 for the arm64 server (sbsa) toolkit, the last CUDA that builds for Maxwell.
inference.notes: Maxwell needs NVIDIA's proprietary kernel module, and on non-coherent PCIe (RK3588) that module must be patched (the m10-arm guide: driver 580.95.05 aarch64, uncached system memory). The M10 is four GPUs: llama.cpp splits a model across them with --split-mode layer. vLLM does not support Maxwell.

retraining.summary: PyTorch on the ARM CPU: PyTorch's aarch64 CUDA wheels target current server GPUs, not Maxwell.
retraining.notes: Train on another computer and serve the result here.

notes: Untested on real hardware: the steps follow the m10-arm guide, which is itself untested on an M10.
